artworks.title: Semiramis Building Babylon
artworks.description: Degas' early history painting: Semiramis surveys the rising walls of Babylon — the legendary queen as nineteenth-century builder of empire.

artworks.title: Semiramis Receiving Word of the Revolt of Babylon
artworks.description: Guercino's canvas: the queen interrupted at her toilet by news of revolt — Baroque theatre for the ruler who would not delay justice for vanity.

artworks.title: Ninus Handing the Crown to Semiramis
artworks.description: Reni's transfer of the crown: Ninus yields power to Semiramis — Bolognese elegance for the legendary succession that made her queen of Assyria.

artworks.title: The Oath of Semiramis
artworks.description: Cortona's Ashmolean composition: Semiramis and the oath that seals her rule — High Baroque rhetoric for the Babylonian queen of Greek legend.

artworks.title: Semiramis Called to Arms
artworks.description: Stella's Lyon canvas: Semiramis rising from her toilet to answer the call of war — the same anecdote Guercino painted, in French classical calm.

films.title: Queen of Babylon
films.description: Italian peplum casting Semiramis as screen queen of Babylon — mid-century cinema's take on the legendary builder and warrior.

films.title: I Am Semiramis
films.description: Another Italian historical spectacle with Semiramis at its centre — the Assyrian queen as 1960s sword-and-sandal heroine.

music.title: Semiramide
music.description: Rossini's Venetian opera — Semiramis as bel canto queen of Babylon, still the figure's most famous stage afterlife.

popCulture.title: Semiramis
popCulture.description: Legendary queen of Assyria and builder of Babylon in Greek historiography — Diodorus' heroine, Rossini's diva.
